issues.legal_issue: A decision made by a decision-maker continuing under a repealed planning scheme is not appealable to the appellate body established by a replacement scheme unless the decision-maker or the appeal process is brought within that replacement scheme.
material_facts: A decision-maker was appointed under the former planning law and made decisions after that law was repealed.
The repeal-saving provision continued the decision-maker’s appointment and pending proceedings, but did not continue the former appellate tribunal.
The replacement law established a new decision-maker and a new appellate body.
The former decision-maker was not expressly appointed to the replacement office.
Appeals from the former decision-maker’s decisions were filed with the new appellate body.
issues.conclusion: The new appellate body had no jurisdiction to hear the appeals, and its orders on them were without jurisdiction.
issues.legal_principle: The saving provision in section 90 of the Bombay Town Planning Act, 1954 continued the former arbitrator’s appointment and proceedings before that arbitrator, but did not continue the former Tribunal of Arbitration. Under the Bombay Town Planning Act, 1915, sections 30–33 provided for the arbitrator and the Tribunal of Arbitration; under the 1954 Act, sections 31–35 provided for a Town Planning officer and a Board of Appeal. The former arbitrator did not become a Town Planning officer without an express appointment, and the Board of Appeal could hear appeals only from decisions of a Town Planning officer. The Court noted that later Maharashtra legislation expressly included a continued arbitrator within references to a Town Planning officer, but no equivalent legislative or governmental action had been taken in Gujarat. No earlier cases were relied on.

rule.if: appeal_from_decision_under_repealed_scheme and former_decision_maker_continued and former_appeal_body_not_continued and not former_decision_maker_appointed_to_replacement_office

predicates.appeal_from_decision_under_repealed_sche: A party filed an appeal from a decision made under a planning scheme established by a law that was later repealed.
predicates.former_decision_maker_continued: The former decision-maker’s appointment or pending proceedings continued after repeal.
predicates.former_appeal_body_not_continued: The repeal-saving arrangement did not continue the former appellate body.
predicates.former_decision_maker_appointed_to_repla: The former decision-maker was expressly appointed to the corresponding office under the replacement scheme.
predicates.new_appellate_body_lacks_jurisdiction: The appellate body established by the replacement scheme has no jurisdiction to hear the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appeal is brought from a decision under a repealed scheme, the former decision-maker continues, the former appeal body does not, and the decision-maker is not appointed to the replacement office, the new appellate body lacks jurisdiction.
